Y gives each relief its own date, includes a colour legend and keeps ghost trails of the earlier routes, so a viewer can follow who sailed, when, and to where. X only shows a static '1780–82' and has no legend.

tra_loi.from: Gibraltar (Allied HQ). Early frames show civilians leaving. In the last frame, Allied forces arrive from the Atlantic, off the left edge of the map.
tra_loi.route: Gibraltar to Casablanca (civilians). Gibraltar to Tangier. Gibraltar to London, Jamaica and Madeira. Allied landings at Casablanca, Oran and Algiers (red arrows from the west), plus aircraft to Oran.
tra_loi.where: Gibraltar, at the southern tip of Spain at the Strait, shown with a red dot. It is hard to find in frame 1 because it is small.

why_split: The 1940 civilian evacuations from Gibraltar and the Nov 1942 Allied landings (Operation Torch) are different stories with different directions of travel, so cramming them into one pan makes the viewer relearn the map.

A 1940 civilian evacuation and a 1942 Allied invasion are two different stories, 2.5 years apart, with different directions of movement and different actors, and the camera jump between them makes the map read as a different place.

The 1940 evacuation and the Nov 1942 Torch landings are different stories, with different directions, scales and framing, and 2.5 years apart. Putting both in one moving shot makes the camera zoom out and drag the viewer through unrelated routes.
